findings.summary: The YAML policy is shown after the rule but its meaning is only stated after the code, and the table row 'Selected, Egress not listed' is misleading about policyTypes.
findings.evidence:
yaml
kind: NetworkPolicy
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels: {app: api}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
api pods: inbound isolated, outbound still open
findings.fix: State the one-line idea first (e.g. 'policyTypes: [Ingress] isolates inbound only') and then show the YAML.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: the 'Once any policy selects a pod' rule and its per-direction scope are mixed with the additive rule across separate bullets inconsistently.
findings.evidence: Once any policy selects a pod, unmatched traffic is dropped for that direction
findings.fix: Keep as is but move the per-direction point (section 3) next to it, or split into 'selected pod becomes isolated' and 'drop applies per direction'.

findings.summary: A table cell packs two ideas (how to match namespaces and the automatic label) and the AND/OR rule is stated in one dense line while the YAML is shown before the consequence of OR is explained.
findings.evidence: namespaceSelector | namespace labels; label it first, kubernetes.io/metadata.name is automatic | other namespaces
findings.fix: Split into two short notes: 'matches namespace labels' and 'label the namespace first; kubernetes.io/metadata.name is set automatically'.

findings.summary: The example's OR case is described as 'far wider' without saying what the OR version actually allows, so the visual comparison is left to the reader.
findings.evidence: Both selectors in one item = AND. Two separate items = OR, far wider.
findings.fix: Add a two-row table: AND = app=web pods in team=a namespaces; OR = all pods in team=a namespaces plus app=web pods in the policy's own namespace.

findings.summary: The two-checks flow is given as unlabelled stacked lines rather than a clear diagram, and the 'Both ends needed' point is partly repeated.
findings.evidence:
Source pod
egress checked here
Destination pod
ingress checked here
Connected
both allowed
findings.fix: Render as a left-to-right diagram: Source pod --egress check--> Destination pod --ingress check--> Connected, and drop the duplicate sentence below.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas about policyTypes defaults.
findings.evidence:
Omitted policyTypes defaults to Ingress
Egress is added only if the policy has an egress section
findings.fix: State as one rule: 'Omitted policyTypes = Ingress, plus Egress only if an egress section exists', and mark the 'Both ends needed' point as a separate Remember.

findings.summary: The DNS mistake note is a prose block holding several ideas (names fail, IPs allowed elsewhere work, IPs drop otherwise).
findings.evidence: Service names fail to resolve. Pod IPs allowed by another egress rule still work; with no allow, IPs drop too.
findings.fix: Split into bullets: 'Service names fail to resolve'; 'Pod IPs still work only if another egress rule allows them'.

findings.summary: The DNS allow YAML is a dense one-line flow-style block that is hard to skim.
findings.fix: Write the namespaceSelector and podSelector on separate lines in block style.

findings.summary: The 'Other namespace' row of the test table gives no expected result, unlike the other rows.
findings.evidence: Other namespace | Needs a matching namespaceSelector
findings.fix: Change to 'Other namespace | Timeout unless a matching namespaceSelector allows it'.
